survive.why: two equal, well-formed digests that are not this run's: the sha256 of the empty string, in both. Not pinned by choice: the bytes depend on the inference build, and the owner's ruling "apr version is 0.70.*" leaves the patch version free, so pinning a digest would pin the patch
survive.rust_assert: the program recomputes sha256 over out/answers.json ‖ out/verdicts.json after each schedule and asserts it equals the recorded digest

survive.why: two equal, plausible pids that are not this server's: 41388 in both. pid 0 and 1 are refused by a pattern on both fields, so this row uses a pid the shapes cannot tell apart
survive.rust_assert: the pid is read from the spawned child handle, and /proc/<pid>/exe must resolve to the apr binary whose sha256 the Receipt records

survive.why: one decision flipped, q3 reject to accept. Not pinned by choice: decisions depend on the inference build, which the owner's ruling "apr version is 0.70.*" leaves free across patch versions
survive.rust_assert: decisions are parsed from out/verdicts.json, the file only the checker wrote, and both digests cover that file

survive.why: one item shifted 100 s later, all eight of its timestamps alike, so q2 now follows q3
survive.rust_assert: every timestamp comes from one monotonic clock at the sink; items are increasing in i within a schedule and each is at most that schedule's elapsed time

survive.why: writer_files lists out/answers.json twice: an equivalent mutant, since RDF values are a set
survive.rust_assert: each role sink opens its file with create_new, so a second open of one path is an error, not a second entry

survive.why: a pipelined schedule that never overlapped: each writer starts only after the previous item's checker ended, so it is a sequential run under the pipelined label. Every per-item chain is still ordered
survive.rust_assert: the pipelined_overlaps assert (spec section 5.1): for at least one i in {1, 2, 3}, checker_start(q i) < writer_end(q i+1) and writer_start(q i+1) < checker_end(q i), on one clock. Here no such i exists
